ranking.placement: the mean of a candidate's rank over the four kinds, lowest first; ties go to the smaller mean error after the change, then to the candidate id
ranking.why: the four questions a trust benchmark asks, in this order: did the monitor ever notice (a model that never notices is the failure this suite exists to find, so a missed case outranks every other column); was it wrong after the change (the truth column -- a model that notices in four readings and is fifteen times further from the plant is not the more trustworthy one); how many readings did it take to notice (the headline metric of the issue); how often does it cry wolf (a monitor that alarms on everything detects everything, and this is the column that says so). The error column is compared with the resolution below, and so is the false-alarm column, so that a kind where every model misses the change by the same amount is decided by the delay instead of by the last digit
